title: Conditions
objective: Make decisions with if, else if, else, the ternary operator and switch
story: We're approaching the Loop Moon! In space you have to make decisions all the time: warn if fuel is low, wait if the weather is bad. Today we give your code the power to **make decisions**.

sections.title: if and else
else if: more than two options
The ternary operator: a short decision
switch and truthiness

examples.title: Fuel warning
examples.note: Set fuel to 50 and run it again.

examples.title: Ternary operator

tasks.title: Oxygen alarm
tasks.prompt:
If `oxygen` is **less than** 30, `status` should be "alarm", otherwise "normal". Use `if`/`else`.

(The code creates `status` as empty first; you give it a value depending on the condition.)

tasks.title: Grade calculator
tasks.prompt:
Decide the letter `grade` from `score`:

- 85 and above: `"A"`
- 70 and above: `"B"`
- 50 and above: `"C"`
- otherwise: `"D"`
hints: Start with the biggest limit: if (score >= 85)

tasks.title: Day or night?
tasks.prompt: If the hour is between 7 and 19 (7 included, 19 not), `mode` should be "day", otherwise "night". This time use the **ternary operator** (`? :`).

challenge.title: Planet guide
challenge.prompt:
Use `switch` to give `info` a value depending on `planet`:

- `"Mercury"` → `"The closest planet"`
- `"Mars"` → `"The red planet"`
- `"Jupiter"` → `"The biggest planet"`
- otherwise: `"Unknown planet"`
hints: Every case must end with break;
default: runs for every other case.

project_task.title: Game state
project_task.prompt:
At any moment the game is in one of three states. Give `message` a value with conditions:

- If lives is `0`: `"Game over!"`
- Otherwise, if there are `10` or more stars: `"Congratulations, you win!"`
- In any other case: say how many stars are left, for example `"Keep going! 2 stars left."` (calculate the number)
hints: Stars left: 10 - stars; write it with a template string.
